newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. insurance firm moves home in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: U.S. insurance firm moves home in Shanghai.

text.p: A major U.S. insurance firm on Thursday returned to its original home on Shanghai's famous waterfront Bund, taking out a lease on the building that housed its headquarters before the Communist takeover in 1949.

American International Assurance Co (AIA), a subsidiary of American International Group, signed a 30-year contract on the eight-storey building, constructed in 1921 as the North China Herald Building, a company statement said.
Most of the other banks and trading houses along the Bund, once the most famous thoroughfare in Asia, have now been rented out or sold.
But the Shanghai city government, which originally had dreams of making a fortune by renting or selling the buildings back to their original owners, has been largely disappointed.

The Hongkong & Shanghai Bank, after two years of negotiations, turned down the opportunity to take back its magnificent former headquarters, the centrepiece of the row of structures lining the foreshore of the Huangpu River.
The building was rented out last week to a local bank, the Shanghai Pudong Development Bank.
AIA was founded in Shanghai in 1931 and is now a major international insurance concern.
It reopened its Shanghai branch in 1992, the first foreign insurance company allowed to do both life and non-life insurance business in China since 1949.
